en: The Ritual Manual of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva,
translated by Śubhakarasiṃha of Central India by Imperial Decree.
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha was on Mount Mālādhāra, together with immeasurable [bodhisattvas].

The Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha was surrounded by a great assembly of ten koṭis of bhikṣus and bhikṣuṇīs, as well as the eight classes of devas, nāgas, and other spirits and ghosts, numbering in the hundreds of thousands, who had gathered to hear him preach the Dharma.
At that time, within the great assembly, there was a Mahāsattva named Kṣitigarbha.
He bared his right shoulder, placed his right knee upon the ground,
joined his palms in reverence, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
I speak this divine mantra desiring to benefit all sentient beings.
I only pray that the World-Honored One, out of compassion and pity, will grant permission to speak this divine mantra.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, saying,
"You all should quickly speak for the benefit of all sentient beings.
Thereupon, Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva ascended into the void and, offering praise, took refuge in the World-Honored One.
While in mid-air, he also manifested immeasurable supernormal powers and, with a divine voice, spoke this mantra:
Oṃ amata-vimala-kūṭe kūṭe samanta svāhā. Then he spoke the heart-mantra.
Oṃ jvalamantre svāhā. Next is the Heart-to-Heart Mantra:
Oṃ khehe. As soon as this mantra is uttered, the great Bodhisattvas of the Ten Stages and others [are moved].
They lost their original minds and became deluded;
the devas, nāgas, the eight classes of beings, yakṣas, and spirits fled in terror, falling prostrate upon the ground.
The sun, moon, and stars lost their radiance and were obscured from the sky.
Rainy showers of precious flowers fell in profusion.
Though one were to recite this mantra for the duration of an eon, its power could not be fully described.
Next, the method for painting an image is explained.
He assumes the form of a śrāvaka,
wearing a kāṣāya robe that neatly covers his left shoulder,
and holds in his left hand a full-blown flower.
His right hand bestows fearlessness and he sits upon a lotus flower.
Furthermore, seated upon the crown of the head of the Great Being (Mahāsattva), he wears a celestial crown and a monastic robe (kāṣāya);
his left hand holds a lotus bud.

With the right hand as before, place it upon the nine-tiered lotus pedestal (*padmāsana*). The tradition states that "nine tiers" refers to nine layers, or alternatively, to the central platform of an eight-petaled lotus.
Next, explain the mudrā and mantra; for the mudrā, join the two palms in the *tripuṭa* gesture.
Place the palms facing inward with the fingers coming together.
The mantra is:
Oṃ jñānamati svāhā. Next, the seal of universal offering is explained.
The two hands form the *tripuṭa* [mudrā];
the *dhyāna* and *jñāna* fingers are positioned as if coming and going.
Oṃ naṃ ja maṇi svāhā. Next, the general mudrā is explained in summary.
Two wings, three *puṭa*.
With the power of progress, standing, coming, and going.
The mantra says:
Oṃ bhañjiye svāhā. Next is the seal for requesting praise:
with both hands in the *tri-puṭa* [gesture], move the fingers of the thumbs forward and backward, then dismiss them; while visualizing the hand in *dhyāna-mudrā*, snap the thumb.
Furthermore, the method for accomplishment is taught:
if one desires to attain great merit,
one should perform seventy thousand *homa* offerings using *agaru* wood while maintaining mindfulness.
If one intends to bring the five grains to fruition,
one should perform homa with rice grains and flowers.
If one intends for others to attain merit and virtue, [one should likewise perform homa].
One should perform homa with soil from the hearth of such a person's house.
If one desires to attain a high position or the two virtues,
one should perform homa with *biri* flowers.
If one intends to subdue enemies throughout successive lifetimes,
perform *homa* using *kaṇṭaka* wood.
If one intends to subdue malevolent spirits or those of heterodox families, [perform *homa* with the same].
If one performs homa with poisonous substances,
madness and chronic illnesses will be cured.
Perform homa with lotus seeds and grasses.
Thirty thousand recitations.
If one intends to extinguish sins, generate wholesome roots, and ensure rebirth in Sukhāvatī after death, perform *homā* with grass thirty thousand times.
If one intends that the curses of wicked people should return to those very persons, [perform the same].
Cast bitter grass (*kaṭuka*) into the fire and perform thirty thousand *homa* offerings;
if one recites this, one will obtain immeasurable fruits of honor and emoluments.
Perform thirty thousand *homa* offerings with the white-flowered bird-grass (*śuklapuṣpavihaṅgā*).
If one wishes to contemplate the merit of the wealth of wisdom through samādhi,
one should perform thirty thousand homa offerings with *kuru* grass.
If one wishes to contemplate the transformation and deliverance of all sentient beings, causing them to leave suffering and attain happiness, [one should likewise perform this].
Perform thirty thousand homa offerings with white mustard seeds.
If one intends to transform and deliver sentient beings in Buddha-less worlds,
perform twenty-one thousand homa offerings with śigru grass.
If one wishes for the five grains to grow in a parched field,
one should empower an old radish and scatter the empowered powder.
If one suffers from ten thousand ailments,
perform thirty thousand *homā* with *nuxiaocao* (Eclipta alba).
If one suffers from the various ailments of the three yin and four heats, [perform the same].
From this point forward, regarding the various types of grass homa:
if a husband and wife are in discord,
performing thirty thousand recitations of the *bīja-grass homa* will bring about their reconciliation.
If one's evil friends oppose one's true friends,
perform thirty thousand *homā* offerings with rattan leaves and grass on the eighth or fourteenth day of the waxing moon.
The Ritual Manual of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva: If one practices the dharma for fifteen days or more, accomplishment will certainly be attained.
